chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him):
he said: the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How excellent a shroud (kafan) is the hullah, and how excellent a sacrificial animal (udhiyyah) is the horned ram.'

The proper interpretation of this report is that we should take it as a type of taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the 'amma (Sunnis). The report we cited previously is consistent with the narrations we presented in the commentary on the washing of the deceased (ghusl al-mayyit) in our major book.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah — precautionary dissimulation; al-Tusi's hermeneutical tool for reconciling hadiths that conform to Sunni norms
key_terms.الْحُلَّةُ: hullah — a two-piece garment set used as a burial shroud; its praise here contradicts the Shia ruling requiring only cotton
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: 'amma — Shia technical term designating the Sunni majority
key_terms.كِتَابِنَا الْكَبِيرِ: our major book — al-Tusi's reference to al-Tahdhib al-Ahkam, his larger hadith compendium of which al-Istibsar is the abridgement

ai.seo_question: Why does Sheikh al-Tusi in al-Istibsar interpret the hadith praising the hullah as a kafan as a form of taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith, attributed to the Prophet (SAWW) via Imam 'Ali (AS) through a chain that includes the Sunni transmitter Isma'il al-Sakkuni, praises the hullah (a two-piece garment) as the best kafan and the horned ram as the best sacrificial animal. Sheikh al-Tusi — in the chapter establishing that only cotton is permissible for the kafan — interprets this narration as having been delivered under taqiyyah, since it conforms to Sunni jurisprudential norms, and defers to his larger compendium al-Tahdhib al-Ahkam for the authoritative Shia ruling.
